articles.title: Fire Starting
articles.content: Gather tinder (dry leaves, bark), kindling (small sticks), and fuel (logs). Create a teepee or log cabin fire lay. Use matches, lighter, ferro rod, or bow-drill friction method. Shield from wind. Never leave unattended.
steps: Build a teepee or log cabin fire lay
Ignite with matches, lighter, ferro rod, or friction

articles.title: Water Purification
articles.content: Boil water for at least 1 minute (3 minutes above 6,500 ft). Use purification tablets or chlorine dioxide drops. Solar disinfection: clear bottle in direct sunlight for 6 hours. Filter through cloth first to remove sediment.
steps: Boil for 1 minute (3 minutes above 6,500 ft)
Use purification tablets or chlorine dioxide
Solar disinfection: clear bottle in sun for 6 hours
Filter through cloth to remove sediment

articles.title: Shelter Building
articles.content: Find natural windbreaks (rock faces, fallen trees). Build lean-to with branches at 45 degrees. Insulate ground with leaves/pine needles. Keep shelter small to retain body heat. Ensure ventilation if using fire nearby.
steps: Insulate the ground with leaves/pine needles
Keep it small to retain heat
Ensure ventilation if using fire nearby

articles.title: Edible Plants
articles.content: Only eat plants you can positively identify. Safe: dandelion (all parts), clover, cattail (roots/shoots), pine needles (tea), chickweed. Avoid: milky sap, umbrella-shaped flowers, almond scent, three-leaved growth, white/yellow berries.
steps: Only eat plants you can positively identify
Safe: dandelion, clover, cattail, pine needles, chickweed
Avoid: milky sap, umbrella flowers, almond scent
Avoid three-leaved growth and white/yellow berries

articles.title: SOS Signals
articles.content: Three of anything: fires, whistle blasts, mirror flashes. Ground-to-air: use contrasting materials, minimum 10ft letters. Mirror signal toward aircraft. At night, use bright fires. Universal distress: SOS (... --- ...) in Morse code.
steps: Three of anything: fires, whistles, flashes

articles.title: Morse Code
articles.content: International communication system using dots and dashes. SOS = ... --- ... Key letters: E=. T=- A=.- I=.. M=-- N=-. Useful for emergency signaling with light, sound, or tapping.
steps: Signal with light, sound, or tapping

articles.title: Navigation Without Tools
articles.content: Sun rises in east, sets in west. North Star (Polaris) indicates north in the northern hemisphere. Moss often grows thicker on north side of trees. Follow waterways downstream toward civilization. Leave trail markers.
steps: Moss grows thicker on the north side of trees

articles.title: Cardinal Directions
articles.content: North, South, East, West. The sun rises in the east and sets in the west. Compass points to magnetic north. True north differs from magnetic north by the declination angle.
steps: True north differs by the declination angle

articles.title: CPR Basics
articles.content: To perform CPR: Check responsiveness, call emergency services, push hard and fast in the center of the chest at 100-120 compressions per minute, give rescue breaths if trained. Continue until help arrives or an AED is available.
steps: Continue until help arrives or an AED is available

articles.title: Bleeding Control
articles.content: Apply direct pressure with clean cloth. Elevate wound above heart. Apply pressure bandage. For severe limb bleeding, apply tourniquet 2-3 inches above wound. Do not remove soaked cloths—add more on top.
steps: Apply direct pressure with clean cloth
Tourniquet 2-3 inches above severe limb wounds
Do not remove soaked cloths—add more on top

articles.title: Burns Treatment
articles.content: Cool burn immediately with cool (not cold) running water for 10-20 minutes. Cover with sterile non-stick dressing. Do not apply ice, butter, or toothpaste. Seek medical help for burns larger than palm size or on face/joints/genitals.
steps: Do not apply ice, butter, or toothpaste
Seek help for large burns or burns on face/joints/genitals

articles.title: Shock Treatment
articles.content: Lay person down with legs elevated 12 inches. Keep warm with blankets. Do not give food or water. Monitor breathing. If unconscious but breathing, place in recovery position. Call emergency services immediately.
steps: Do not give food or water
Monitor breathing; recovery position if unconscious

articles.title: Fracture Splinting
articles.content: Immobilize the joint above and below the fracture. Use rigid materials (sticks, boards) padded with cloth. Secure with bandages but don't restrict circulation. Check pulse below splint regularly.
steps: Immobilize joints above and below the fracture
Secure with bandages without restricting circulation
Check pulse below the splint regularly

articles.title: Hypothermia
articles.content: Move to shelter. Remove wet clothing. Warm gradually with blankets, skin-to-skin contact. Give warm sweet drinks if conscious. Do not rub limbs, apply direct heat, or give alcohol. Severe cases: call emergency services.
steps: Do not rub limbs or give alcohol

articles.title: Dehydration
articles.content: Occurs when body loses more fluid than it takes in. Symptoms: thirst, dark urine, dizziness, fatigue. Prevention: drink water regularly, more in heat/exertion. Treatment: oral rehydration salts, sip water slowly.
steps: Symptoms: thirst, dark urine, dizziness, fatigue

articles.title: Wilderness First Aid
articles.content: The practice of medicine in environments where definitive care is delayed. Priorities: scene safety, primary survey (ABCs), secondary survey. Evacuation decisions based on mechanism of injury and patient condition.
steps: Decide on evacuation based on mechanism and condition
